observation_summary: SerializationUtils.clone() throws a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone primitive classes (e.g., int.class).
hypothesis: The custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.resolveClass method fails to handle primitive classes because it only attempts to load them via specific class loaders and does not delegate to the superclass's resolveClass method, which contains the necessary logic to resolve primitive types.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the resolveClass method in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream to include a fallback mechanism that calls super.resolveClass(desc) when the custom class loading attempts fail.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies that the custom override of resolveClass lacks a fallback to the superclass implementation, which is required to handle primitive types correctly as per standard Java ObjectInputStream behavior.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a procedural failure in the custom class resolution logic. The method attempts to resolve classes using specific class loaders but fails to account for primitive types, which are handled by the standard ObjectInputStream. Adding a fallback to the superclass method is a procedural correction to the class resolution algorithm, fitting the Algorithm/Method ODC type.
evidence_used: Bug report description identifying the lack of delegation to super.resolveClass
Stack trace showing ClassNotFoundException during cloning

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a check is missing, the primary issue is the failure of the resolution algorithm to correctly identify primitive types, which is a procedural logic error rather than just a missing guard.
The issue is not a mismatch in the interface contract between components, but an internal failure of the class resolution procedure to handle specific data types.
